Prevention: Select termite-free site by scouting for their signs and remains
Check for termite hills or colonies and destroy if any discovered in the cultivation sites
For small localised areas with infestation, sterilize soil before planting (e.g. with hot water)
Remove plant residues or termite-infested logs from site and burn
Practice deep ploughing and harrowing to expose termites buried in the ground
Distract termites attention by establishing wood lots where they would concentrate away from the field
Practice hand weeding twice at six week intervals
First hand weeding should be done when the rice is three weeks old
Monitoring: Identify termite mounds and pay attention to the rice plant nearest to those mounds for damage signs or cuts on stems
Uproot plants that are suspected of termite attack and burn
Take immediate action when termites are detected
Direct Control: Use hoe weeding or earthing method to expose underground termites
Uproot plants that are suspected of termite attack and burn
Use hot water to kill termites in close locations (holes or colonies)
Allow birds to feed on the termites after destroying termite mounds
Dust wood ash on their pathways to the field
Allow free flow of water in the peripheral drainage to prevent termites entering rice plots
Restrictions: II (Moderately hazardous); Spray around the edges of the field to prevent termites from entering the crop or spot treat infestation within the crop; Application rate 65-70 mls of product (chemical) to 5 litres of water at 4 week intervals (4
